visualReview.notes: Inspected all seven final portable views and the full front frame against the local Qualla museum aerial and inspected supplemental museum front/Warren LeMay side photographs. Restored orange/white shaft, rectangular elevator spine, left spiral stair, three circular balconies and octagonal upper cab remain distinct. Attached two-storey operations block retains two garage bays, horizontal canopies, rounded front bay, outside end stair and separate small aerological cab. Fine tread counts and hidden elevations are generalized.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Inspected all seven final shared views including the north-up placement overlay. Painted metal and plain concrete retain metric UVs; glazing stays portable. Model main frontage and two separate cab outlines agree with generalized map controls. Source/runtime transform, reference-point sampling, unload and material-graph reads pass. Flat shared fixture tests materials/transforms; independent preserved terrain validates ground contact.

mediumFiReview.notes: Inspected all nineteen final medium-fi frames across lights, quality modes, front/back, silhouette and forced levels. Initial street framing cut off the operations block; final context scale 1.6 includes the entire structure. Orange/white rhythm, upper cabin and attached operations remain legible. Skyline omits tiny stair and balcony railings; district retains a simplified spiral ribbon. Synthetic neighboring buildings are a style fixture, not Ford Island. No physical-device performance claim.

fidelityReview.scope: Restored Ford Island control/water tower, attached operations building and small aerological cab; hangars, aircraft and interiors excluded.
fidelityReview.notes: Accepted original medium-fi restored control tower with connected operations block and small aerological cab. Local Qualla aerial supplies site context only; inspected museum front and Warren LeMay 2022 side photograph supply architectural evidence. Supplementary review records attribution and URLs. Published 158 ft and 168 ft descriptions are inconsistent; approximately 48.2 m shaft transition and 51.2 m upper deck are an interpretation, not a survey. Hidden windows, detailed rail/tread counts, equipment, interiors and neighboring hangars are excluded or simplified. Photography is not redistributed.

runtimeLodReview.notes: All four current hash-bound levels pass strict budgets and were visually inspected: skyline 992, district 3338, street 13878, closeup 16666 triangles. Skyline/district/street are authored. The initial skyline exceeded 1000 by four triangles; small canopy/parapet simplification brought it under budget while retaining the antenna. Error limits are declared authoring budgets, not independent mesh-distance measurements.

geometryValidation.notes: Exact source regeneration, ordinary import verification, four current LOD checks and strict medium-fi audit passed. Source bundle, scene and terrain schemas pass; terrain PNG round-trip error is recorded above. No independent Khronos-validator run is claimed.

limitations: Original medium-fi restored exterior, using inspected local Qualla aerial for site context and museum/Warren LeMay supplemental front and side photographs for architectural evidence; not a measured survey.

Museum sources describe 158 ft tower height and 168 ft observation access differently. The recipe approximates a 48.2 m shaft/tank transition and 51.2 m upper deck; individual levels, cabin roof and antenna heights are estimates.

Orange/white restored exterior represents the modern tower, not the incomplete camouflage-era 1941 structure. Spiral tread count, hidden rear windows, rail subdivisions, doors and rooftop equipment are simplified.
Includes the attached operations building and small aerological cab. Hangars, museum aircraft, interiors, vegetation and other site structures are excluded.
Reference photographs are viewed for research and are not embedded or redistributed. Generalized map geometry and host terrain require review when using another elevation dataset.
